tests.failure_mode: POST /v1/git/rollback deletes a file outside the repository through a symlinked parent directory, deletes directories, accepts traversal, mis-classifies paths (restore vs unstage vs untracked), or leaves the index/worktree un-restored. Wave F-E: a path that is a file in HEAD but now a directory in the worktree is routed to git restore (checkout-force semantics), which replaces the directory and deletes everything inside it, including ignored/untracked user files.
tests.importance: Destructive filesystem operation: an escaped delete removes user data outside the workspace; wrong classification destroys or keeps the wrong changes.

nearest_retained.why_insufficient: Retained auth_matrix_git_stage_rejects_non_relative_paths checks only lexical ../ and absolute rejection on /v1/git/stage; it cannot detect symlink-parent escape, directory deletion, or rollback classification/restore effects.

tests.oracle: Default-flags request (no delete flags): unstaged [added.txt], deleted [], skipped exactly [untracked.txt=untracked], both files still on disk. Full-flags request: exact restored/unstaged/deleted arrays and exact sorted skipped list (dir=directory, dir/inner.txt=unchanged, link/victim.txt=symlink_parent, swap=directory); outside victim file content unchanged and link still present; tracked.txt index+worktree equal HEAD; added.txt removed from index and disk; untracked.txt deleted; ../escape.txt returns 400. Wave F-E: right after the full-flags call, swap/precious.secret (an ignored file inside the directory that replaced the HEAD file swap) still reads 'ignored work' (asserted before any other response check).
tests.prerequisites: Victim file exists outside the root before the call; link is a real symlink to the outside dir; tracked.txt has distinct staged and worktree edits; added.txt staged and not in HEAD; untracked.txt exists; dir/inner.txt unchanged and tracked. Wave F-E: swap is committed in HEAD, then gets a staged edit (so status reports a change), then is replaced on disk by a directory holding only an ignored file (exclude *.secret; status_should_ignore asserted true) — a directory holding only ignored files is reported as a deleted file, which the old classifier routes to git restore.

tests.failure_mode: A subagent's cleared LIVE session context cap (thread.context_tokens_cap None, implicit full-window launch) is overwritten at persistence time by the frozen launch config (Some(n_ctx)), e.g. when the detached frozen-config save path runs instead of the runner-owned live session, so the durable trajectory permanently carries an artificial cap; related regressions are an explicit cap lost on reload or an implicit window recorded as an explicit cap.
tests.importance: Durable persistence of the optional context cap decides the child's context window and auto-compression threshold after resume: a spurious persisted cap permanently shrinks an implicit-window subagent, and a dropped explicit cap lets it exceed the user's limit.

tests.oracle: Implicit launch: n_ctx=1,000,000, thread cap None, auto_compression 900,000, serde round-trip config cap None. Explicit 300,000: thread cap Some(300000), auto_compression 270,000, legacy config without the discriminator keeps Some(300000). Caps above the model window (1,000,001) and zero are rejected. Live refresh: runner session cap 300,000 sets ccx.n_ctx 300,000; 2,000,000 clamps to model 1,000,000; cleared cap restores 1,000,000 for Unsupervised and a Supervised policy leaves n_ctx untouched. Failed-run save through the real save path reloads from disk with thread.context_tokens_cap == None and contains the provider-failed event message.
tests.prerequisites: make_test_gcx isolated cache with injected caps for test/1m and test/200k chat models, AppState from the gcx, temporary workspace folder, a real stateful runner-owned session installed by install_stateful_subchat_session and put in Generating state; progress messages seeded with one user message.
tests.shipping_implementation: Calls production apply_launch_context_window, stateful_thread_from_config, SubchatConfig serde/context_tokens_cap, install_stateful_subchat_session, refresh_live_context_window and save_failed_subchat_trajectory, which runs production save_subchat_trajectory (save_through_runner_session, else frozen-config save_trajectory_as_with_intent_checked) and loads the saved file with load_trajectory_for_chat; no test-local reimplementation of the cap logic.
tests.determinism: Temporary directories and isolated make_test_gcx cache; in-process only, no network, credentials, sleeps or timing races; runs in about 0.1s; exact equality assertions on integers.

Several are pure functions, but the live-refresh and persistence scenarios need the real session and filesystem, so they are kept together rather than duplicating that fixture.
